page: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Dadv6 family. It operates on the x86_64 architecture and is driven by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor running at up to 3.7 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The instance exposes 48 vCPUs distributed across 24 dedicated physical cores with multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises a 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a 32 MB L3 cache, backed by vector and instruction extensions including AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, and AVX-512 BF16.

The configuration provides 192.0 GB of total RAM, sustaining a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 4.0 GB per vCPU. Hardware resources also include 2,832 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed scratch space directly on the host node. There are no discrete GPUs allocated to this instance profile, and complimentary public IPv4 addresses are omitted.

Benchmark outcomes show top-tier computational capacity across both single-threaded and multithreaded operations. The instance registered a Geekbench single-core score of 2,103.0 and a multi-core score of 20,566.0, supplemented by a PassMark CPU score of 62,724.38 and a stress-ng multi-core result of 73,828.07. Extended instruction support is underscored by strong performances in AES encryption tests and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 286.74 GB/sec. Memory subsystem testing reflects 3,648.63 GB/sec cached small-block throughput, falling to average ranks under larger, uncached reads at 116.44 GB/sec.

The hardware profile balances raw thread capacity and fast local NVMe capacity against moderate uncached memory bandwidth. Synthetic database benchmarks reach 22,127.37 operations on PassMark and 63.99 million Redis SET operations per second. While smaller LLM inference profiles perform adequately, larger multi-billion parameter model execution is constrained by CPU memory bus bandwidth and the absence of GPU acceleration. The server fits high-concurrency relational and NoSQL databases, enterprise CI/CD pipelines, large compilation tasks, and microservice aggregation layers.
description: Microsoft Azure D48ads_v6 is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores derived from an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor clocked at 3.7 GHz. Configured with 192.0 GB of memory and 2,832 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, it pairs high core density with fast node-local data access. Benchmarks demonstrate strong CPU throughput, scoring 20,566.0 on Geekbench multi-core and registering 63.99 million Redis SET operations per second. Supported instruction flags include AVX-512 and hardware encryption primitives, enabling rapid execution of compiled workloads and multi-threaded decompression. Without dedicated GPUs, large-scale deep learning generation scales poorly, though smaller inference tasks remain functional. The instance provides an efficient hardware footprint for high-throughput enterprise databases, distributed caching, CI/CD compilation workloads, and intensive backend web services.
